subject: Acme: Long-context eval follow-up & recommended models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme discovery — long-context recap & recommended next steps

Hi Jane / John,

Thanks again for the 45-minute discovery earlier today — really helpful to learn about the document ingestion pipeline and the two main use cases you called out (legal contract summarization across multi-file evidence bundles, and long-thread customer support summarization). Quick recap + recommended next steps so we can align on a PoC and model fit evaluation.

Summary of needs we heard:
- Typical doc bundle: 10-200 files, average 150k tokens total per bundle, lots of PDF text + OCR edge cases.
- Key output: high-fidelity extractive + abstractive summaries with citation links to original docs, and an ability to answer follow-up Qs without losing context.
- SLOs: sub-750ms per incremental token where interactive, or batched throughput for offline summarization.
- Security: data must remain within Acme VPC; audit logs required.

Initial model fit recommendations (for long-context eval):
1) Redwood-70B-Chat (8-bit quant) — best balance of long-context modeling and fidelity for abstractive summaries; strong at instruction-following when prompt-engineered.
2) Redwood-13B-Long — faster and cheaper for batched summarization; recommend as fallback for high-volume runs.
3) Mistral-7B-Instruct (context-extended variant) — good for extractive QA with smaller latencies.

Why these: we ran a small internal long-context eval on a redacted bundle similar to what you described. The 70B maintained better citation fidelity past 64k tokens when we used prefix-preserving caching and chunked KV caching. The 13B variant performs well when you accept a two-pass summarization (chunk + synthesize).

Key evaluation points we propose for the PoC:
- Truncation behavior: measure where key facts drop out across model variants (we saw drift starting ~72k in a naive single-pass; caching + overlap windows pushed usable context to ~120k in our tests).
- Summarization fidelity: gold-set ROUGE + human review on 50 bundles.
- Latency/cost: token-level breakdown and expected per-bundle cost across model variants and quantization levels.

Attachments: I attached the prompt set we used (acme_prompt_set_v3.json) and the initial eval PDF with sample output (acme_long_context_eval_v1.pdf). Also linking the shared spreadsheet with per-example metrics: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-eval-results-acme

Suggested next steps / asks for Acme:
1) Share a small redacted sample bundle (10 bundles) so we can reproduce locally.
2) Confirm whether you want a 1-week pilot (50 bundles) or a 4-week evaluation (250 bundles) — we will size Dedicated capacity for throughput accordingly.
3) Agree on security requirements (NDA, VPC onboarding, KMS) — Rishi is looped for the compliance bits.

Proposed time for a 30-min technical walk-through next week: Wed 3/11 or Thu 3/12 between 10a-2p PT. Let me know what works and I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting a small eval running.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks John — answers inline below and attaching the mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_ACME-2026-289.xlsx):

1) Failure modes at a glance:
- 64k (single-pass naive): early-context facts start to drop out as model overwrites KV cache; hallucinated citations occur when the model tries to reconcile conflicting evidence but lacks the earlier doc tokens.
- 72–90k: performance degrades progressively; if you use a naive attention window you’ll see hallucination and hallucinated dates or references.
- 90–128k with prefix/KV caching + overlap windows: much better. Our tests show that with 4k overlap windows and chunked synthesize passes the 70B maintains citation correctness for ~85% of gold citations on our redacted set.

2) Ballpark cost (per-bundle, 50–200k tokens):
- 70B quantized (single-pass + KV caching): ~$18–$30 per bundle depending on average token count and cache hit rate.
- 13B two-pass (chunk + synthesize): ~$6–$10 per bundle; higher human-review cost but cheaper machine cost.

3) Sandbox + VPC onboarding timeline:
- Standard: 5 business days for VPC peering + KMS integration (assuming Acme infra team provides required network peering info quickly).
- If you need Private (on-prem) deployment, add 3–4 weeks for packaging and validation.

Human evaluation: yes — we will include 2 human reviewers per bundle for the PoC if you confirm. We’ll surface both ROUGE-like metrics and a small rubric for citation fidelity/accuracy.

Attachments included: acme_prompt_set_v3.json (prompt set used), acme_long_context_eval_v1.pdf (redacted example outputs), mutual_action_plan_ACME-2026-289.xlsx (proposed milestones and responsibilities).

I’ve scheduled the technical walk-through for Thu 3/12 11:00 AM PT and sent a calendar invite to your address. Rishi will join to cover security & onboarding.

Best,
Marissa
